$comment: Both implementations must agree here - tools/runner/alphabet.py and web/src/server/tools/detect.ts. Two implementations of one rule are fine; two rules are not, and this corpus is what proves they have not become two rules. Each case exists because it is a way to be wrong, not because it is a way to be right.

01-protein-recA.fasta.why: protein-only residues settle it outright, whatever the counts say

04-ambiguous-short-acgt.fasta.why: a short peptide of only ACGT is genuinely indistinguishable from DNA; no threshold rescues this and guessing here is how BLU-22 happens again

05-aligned-protein.aln.fasta.why: gaps must be stripped before counting, and this is the exact input that must be refused for a nucleotide-only port

06-dna-fastq-protein-looking-quality.fas.why: quality lines are deliberately full of E, F, I, L, P and Q - counting them detects a nanopore run as protein with certain confidence, which was a real bug

07-newick.nwk.why: a tree is not a sequence; a parser that only skips headers eats the taxon names and answers confidently about a file it should refuse
